sets.relationshipLabel: two ends of one spatial axis
sets.explanation: North and south, east and west are the two opposing ends of the same compass axis.

sets.relationshipLabel: a kind of geographic feature and a named example of it
sets.explanation: A strait is a category of waterway and Gibraltar names one; a peninsula is a category of landform and Florida names one.

sets.relationshipLabel: a worker and the tool of their trade
sets.explanation: A surveyor relies on a theodolite and a navigator relies on a sextant, each the defining instrument of their profession.

sets.relationshipLabel: the part that lets the device or system perform its function
sets.explanation: A needle is what actually lets a compass point, just as a satellite is what actually lets GPS locate you.

glossary.definition: A precision instrument on a tripod with a small telescope, used for measuring angles between points.

definitions.definition: The direction that points toward the top of most maps, away from the equator toward the pole.
The direction opposite north, toward the bottom of most maps.
The direction the sun rises from, to the right when you're facing north.
The direction the sun sets in, to the left when you're facing north.
A narrow strip of water connecting two larger seas or bodies of water.
A famous narrow passage of water linking the Atlantic Ocean to the Mediterranean Sea.
A piece of land almost surrounded by water, connected to the mainland on one side.
A well-known strip of land in the southeastern US that juts out into the ocean.
Someone who measures land carefully to map boundaries, elevations, and distances.
A precision instrument on a tripod with a small telescope, used for measuring angles between points.
Someone who figures out a route or position, especially at sea or in the air.
A handheld tool that measures the angle between the horizon and a star or the sun to find your position.
The thin pointer that swings to show which way is which inside a directional tool.
A small device with a pointer that always settles toward magnetic north.
An object orbiting Earth that sends signals down for communication or positioning.
A system that tells you exactly where you are on Earth using signals from space.
